headline: Foggy, dry days through Friday, then a wetter, windier pattern returns early next week.
summary: A strong ridge of high pressure aloft, a dome of high pressure high in the atmosphere, is building over western Washington tonight. It brings clear skies, light winds, and a stretch of dry weather through Friday. Fog will form in the lowlands and river valleys each morning, and it could be freezing in colder spots. Highs will be in the 40s. The ridge fades over the weekend, and light rain and snow showers arrive Saturday evening, with little impact in the mountains. Early next week, a busy stretch of Pacific storm systems takes over. A stronger system Monday into Tuesday could bring widespread rain, breezy winds, strong winds on the coast, and minor coastal flooding at high tide. The wet, breezy pattern continues into midweek, though timing and strength remain uncertain.
changes: Later discussions said confidence in strong coastal winds grew, with gale-force gusts and possible storm-force winds peaking Tuesday. They also added a Saturday evening rain and snow forecast, with snow levels near 2,000 feet, and extended the fog outlook through Friday night.
